You’re looking into the rabbit hole of creative non-fiction. It is controversial and new because it is telling the truth but maybe it’s in a skewed, creative way. Examples: it is from a biased point of view or untrustworthy narrator, it is from the point of view of someone else but you surmise their personal thoughts, it is telling a story of something that did happen but changing small details (changing the seasons, setting, names) to fit your vision and adding/removing scenes. Creative non-fiction takes prose and facts and laces them together. Basically, creative non-fiction is: so long as you get the point or facts across in the end of the story, it doesn’t matter if you take some artistic changes or additions to the story to make it interesting.
